description: Extraction completes in <5 seconds for any scenario with ≤200 files and <30 seconds for any scenario with ≤2000 files, measured end-to-end including Connect-RPC transport and Node sidecar round-trip. Performance regression tests live in CI.

requirements.description: Extraction must complete end-to-end (including Connect-RPC transport and Node sidecar round-trip) within defined time bounds: under 5 seconds for projects with 200 or fewer source files, and under 30 seconds for projects with 2000 or fewer source files. Performance regression tests must run in CI against representative fixture projects. Any commit that causes extraction to exceed these bounds must fail CI. Measurements must be wall-clock time from RPC call initiation to full response receipt.
requirements.title: Extraction Performance SLA with CI Enforcement

validation.notes: Test that performance measurement utilities correctly capture wall-clock time from RPC start to response
Test that the performance test harness generates synthetic TS projects with configurable file counts
TCG-PERF-200: Extract a 200-file representative fixture completes in under 5 seconds end-to-end in CI (p95 across 5 runs)
TCG-PERF-2000: Extract a 2000-file representative fixture completes in under 30 seconds end-to-end in CI (p95 across 3 runs)
CI performance test fails if measured extraction time exceeds SLA thresholds
Performance tests run on a consistent CI runner configuration to avoid environment variance
200-file extraction: p95 < 5 seconds wall-clock including Connect-RPC and sidecar
2000-file extraction: p95 < 30 seconds wall-clock including Connect-RPC and sidecar
Performance regression: CI fails if any run exceeds 110% of the SLA threshold
react-component-library migration tooling operates within acceptable latency for developer feedback loops
Performance SLA is documented in the operator runbook with measurement methodology

title: Performance SLA
